# requireCountable

<link-summary>Returns the value as a countable number, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireCountable() — Returns the value as a countable number, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireCountable(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a non-negative safe integer."
): number;
```

A value that can serve as a quantity, a length or a zero-based index: a whole number, not negative, and small enough that integer arithmetic on it is still exact.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                          | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                            | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-negative safe integer."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as a countable number.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                            |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a countable number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireCountable(0); // => 0
requireCountable(42); // => 42
requireCountable(-1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireCountable(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
